title: Add optional id to ChatStreamEnable echoed as requestId
description:
Spec sync to jmap-chat-spec 63e9d08 (diff 0cd3af0..63e9d08). Oracle: the quoted spec text at 63e9d08.

[wss] Add optional id to ChatStreamEnable echoed as requestId
Spec (): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-wss-00.md L185-186: "`id` (String, optional): A client-specified identifier for this message. A `RequestError` caused by this message carries this value as its `requestId` ({{RFC8887}} Section 4.3.4)." L192: "As with `WebSocketPushEnable` ({{RFC8887}}), success is silent and failure produces a `RequestError`. A client that sends several control messages in succession SHOULD give each an `id` ..."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ephemeral.rs:15-39; crate-jmap-chat-server/src/ephemeral.rs:74-83; crate-jmap-chat-client/src/ws.rs:115-122
Now: ChatStreamEnable has no `id` field, so a wire id lands only in `extra`. The server-side docs for from_enable describe the RequestError but do not say to echo the frame's id as requestId. The client has no typed way to set the id or to match it against WsFrame::request_id (which already exists in crate-jmap-base-client/src/ws/mod.rs:140).
Change: Add `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub id: Option<String>` to ChatStreamEnable, and document in from_enable/replace_with that the transport must put enable.id into the RequestError's requestId. Update the client send_stream_enable docs to mention correlation.
